title: An Act to Ensure the Supremacy of Parliament
summary: A traditional pro forma bill introduced at the opening of each session, before debate on the Speech from the Throne, to assert the Legislative Assembly's right to consider matters other than those raised by the Crown. It is not intended to proceed beyond first reading.

title: Acting Conflict of Interest Commissioner Continuation Act
summary: Disapplies the provision of the Members' Conflict of Interest Act under which an acting Conflict of Interest Commissioner ceases to hold office after the Legislative Assembly has sat for 20 days, allowing the acting commissioner to continue in office.

title: Protected Areas of British Columbia Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Protected Areas of British Columbia Act to move several ecological reserves into the Act's schedules, change the boundaries and sizes of several parks, repeal the description of Kilby Park, and rename Enderby Cliffs Park and Maquinna Marine Park with Indigenous names.

title: Business Practices and Consumer Protection Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Business Practices and Consumer Protection Act to prohibit consumer contract terms that bar consumer reviews, prevent class proceedings or require arbitration, and sets new disclosure and cancellation requirements for direct sales, future performance, distance sales, subscription and similar contracts.

title: Budget Measures Implementation Act, 2025
summary: Implements tax and non-tax measures from Budget 2025, including extending the period in which deficits may be forecast to the 2027–2028 fiscal year, changes to the sales tax credit and the BC family benefit, a higher individual limit for the small business venture capital tax credit, and changes to film and television production tax credits.

title: Supply Act (No. 1), 2025
summary: Interim supply bill authorizing government spending from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for part of the 2025–2026 fiscal year until the main budget estimates are approved.

title: Economic Stabilization (Tariff Response) Act
summary: Provides measures in response to U.S. tariffs, including removing barriers to goods and services from other Canadian provinces and territories, authorizing procurement directives, allowing tolls or fees on the use of provincial undertakings, and giving cabinet temporary regulation-making powers to modify enactments, with reports to be tabled in the Legislative Assembly.

title: Carbon Tax Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Carbon Tax Act to set carbon tax rates for fuels to zero starting April 1, 2025, repeals collector and registration requirements for fuel and natural gas sellers, provides for refunds of amounts collected after that date, and adds limited retroactive regulation-making authority.

title: Health Care Costs Recovery Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Health Care Costs Recovery Act to strengthen the government's ability to recover health care costs from wrongdoers, including requiring that the government be notified of third-party claims and giving it subrogated rights against parties entitled to contributions or indemnities.

title: Attorney General Statutes Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Makes amendments to several statutes administered by the Attorney General, including changes to pension entitlements under the Judicial Compensation Act and to provisions of the Land Title Act.

title: Employment Standards Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Employment Standards Act so that, in specified circumstances, employers must not request a sick note for short-term health-related leave, and authorizes related regulations.

title: Motor Vehicle Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Motor Vehicle Act, including lowering the age at which a person can apply for a driver's licence on their own from 19 to 18, adding regulation-making powers on novice drivers and driving experience, requiring prescribed protective gear for motorcycle riders, and restricting electronic device use by learner motorcyclists.

title: Miscellaneous Statutes Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Omnibus bill amending multiple statutes, including notice and hearing requirements under the Wildfire Act, local government development financing, housing supply and local election campaign financing provisions, and amendments affecting the School Act, Professional Governance Act and Wildlife Act.

title: Renewable Energy Projects (Streamlined Permitting) Act
summary: Provides for renewable energy projects to be regulated by the British Columbia Energy Regulator at one of three levels of streamlined permitting, and modifies how the Energy Resource Activities Act and other statutes apply to those projects.

title: Infrastructure Projects Act
summary: Allows cabinet to designate public and other infrastructure projects and authorize streamlining options for designated projects, including streamlined permitting and varying requirements in provincial legislation.

title: Supply Act, 2025–2026
summary: Main supply bill authorizing government spending from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the 2025–2026 fiscal year, as approved through the budget estimates.

title: Intimate Images Protection Statutes Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Civil Resolution Tribunal Act and related statutes to broaden intimate image claims, allow such claims to be brought or continued in Provincial Court, permit legal representation in these claims, and authorize regulations setting monetary limits.

title: Sexual Violence Policy Act
summary: Repeals and replaces the Sexual Violence and Misconduct Policy Act, requiring post-secondary institutions to meet updated policy objectives, establish advisory committees, consult, report annually, make training available and, in some cases, share the outcome of formal allegations with the person who made them.

title: School Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the School Act to expand the authority of boards of education to provide child care programs on board property and changes how costs are described for the fees and revenue boards may collect for those programs.

title: Construction Prompt Payment Act
summary: Establishes a prompt payment scheme for the construction industry, including regular invoicing, payment deadlines and an interim adjudication process for resolving payment disputes.

title: Attorney General Statutes Amendment Act (No. 2), 2025
summary: Amends several statutes, including adding a retroactive tax under the Insurance (Vehicle) Act tied to reimbursements during a specified period, and updating the Public Guardian and Trustee Act's provisions on property guardianship of children, including Indigenous children and agreements with Indigenous authorities.

title: Statutes Act
summary: Replaces existing rules on the publication of provincial statutes, providing for online Acts and online consolidations to be relied on as official versions for evidentiary purposes.

title: Regulations Act
summary: Replaces the Regulations Act with updated requirements for drafting, depositing and publishing regulations online, and provides for online regulations and consolidations to be official versions for evidentiary purposes.

title: Vaping Product Damages and Health Care Costs Recovery Act
summary: Creates a legal framework for the government to sue manufacturers of vaping products to recover health care costs attributed to vaping-related illness.

title: Housing and Municipal Affairs Statutes Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Local Government Act, Vancouver Charter and Short-Term Rental Accommodations Act, including changes to small-scale multi-unit housing zoning requirements, new regulation-making powers over off-street parking requirements, heritage designation transition rules, and a process for local governments to seek extensions to comply.

title: Vancouver Charter Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Vancouver Charter to provide a framework for dissolving the Vancouver Park Board and transferring its responsibilities, assets, liabilities and records to Vancouver City Council.

title: Miscellaneous Statutes Amendment Act (No. 2), 2025
summary: Amends the School Act and Expropriation Act regarding land acquisition and expropriation by boards of education and the francophone education authority, and amends the Community Charter and Vancouver Charter regarding closed council meetings and Indigenous entities.

title: Business Practices and Consumer Protection Amendment Act (No. 2), 2025
summary: Amends the Business Practices and Consumer Protection Act to regulate credit repair services, add consumer rights to place security alerts and credit freezes on credit reports, and update disclosure requirements for certain contracts.

title: Child, Family and Community Service Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Child, Family and Community Service Act to provide for temporary safety plan agreements to protect a child's health or safety while an assessment or investigation is under way or a court order is being sought.

title: Employment Standards (Serious Illness or Injury Leave) Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Employment Standards Act to provide up to 27 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave within a 52-week period for an employee's serious personal illness or injury, with a medical certificate requirement.

title: Energy Statutes Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Allows cabinet to designate agreements under which BC Hydro and First Nations hold ownership interests in parts of the North Coast transmission line, and expands regulation-making authority over electricity service for data storage and processing and other specified uses.

title: Mental Health Amendment Act (No. 2), 2025
summary: Amends the Mental Health Act to extend liability protection to providers of authorized services, care and treatment, and removes the provision deeming involuntary patients to have consented to treatment authorized by a facility director.

title: Low Carbon Fuels Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Low Carbon Fuels Act to reduce compliance units issued for imported renewable fuel that received financial incentives in other jurisdictions, and requires compliance reports to disclose those incentives.

title: Eligibility to Hold Public Office Act
summary: Disqualifies a sitting Member of the Legislative Assembly from also holding local elected office, such as a municipal council seat.

title: Free Trade and Mobility Within Canada Act
summary: Provides for the removal of interprovincial trade barriers between British Columbia and the other provinces and territories.

title: Perinatal and Postnatal Mental Health Strategy Act
summary: Requires the minister to develop a strategy to support perinatal and postnatal mental health in British Columbia.

title: Mental Health Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Mental Health Act to require physicians or nurse practitioners to take reasonable steps to consult a near relative or the person who provided information leading to an apprehension, and requires notice to a near relative before a patient is discharged from a designated facility.

title: Interpretation (Pacific Daylight Time) Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Replaces the Daylight Saving Time Regulation so that British Columbia would remain on Pacific Daylight Time (seven hours behind Greenwich Mean Time) year-round after the second Sunday of March.

title: Greenhouse Gas Industrial Reporting and Control Repeal Act
summary: Repeals the Greenhouse Gas Industrial Reporting and Control Act.

title: Emergency and Disaster Management Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Emergency and Disaster Management Act to require the minister to establish a committee to support the development of a provincial volunteer organization called BC Volunteer Corps.

title: Tax Relief and Tariff Defence Act
summary: Proposes income tax relief and would allow cabinet to remove procedural obstacles to natural resource development, public infrastructure and economic development in response to tariffs and other economic challenges. The bill was ruled out of order.

title: Korean Heritage Month Act
summary: Establishes October as Korean Heritage Month in British Columbia.

title: Zero-Emission Vehicles Repeal Act
summary: Repeals the Zero-Emission Vehicles Act.

title: Income Tax (Grocery Rebate Guarantee) Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Income Tax Act to raise the basic personal amount used in the provincial income tax calculation from $9,713 to $22,462.

title: Drug Use Prevention Education in Schools Act
summary: Provides for drug use prevention education and mandatory anti-drug messaging in schools.

title: Firefighters' Health Act
summary: Requires development of a plan for comprehensive health screening of firefighters, to be tabled in the Legislative Assembly and reviewed every five years, and provides for a review of workers' compensation presumptions for firefighters' occupational diseases such as lung cancer. Reinstated in the 2nd session (2026) at the stage it had reached.

title: Parental Transparency and Age-Appropriate Education Act
summary: Requires the Minister of Education to establish a Committee for Parental Transparency and Age-Appropriateness in Education to review materials in public schools.

title: Professional Reliance Act
summary: Provides for streamlining local government approvals of development projects and reducing their administrative costs, including greater reliance on qualified professionals. Reinstated in the 2nd session (2026) at the stage it had reached.

title: Dashboard Cameras in Commercial Vehicles Act
summary: Provides for the mandatory installation and operation of dashboard cameras in commercial vehicles. Reinstated in the 2nd session (2026) at the stage it had reached.

title: Residential Tenancy Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Residential Tenancy Act to prohibit landlords from raising the rent on a vacant unit above the amount that would have been allowed had the previous tenant stayed.

title: Health Authorities Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Health Authorities Act to require health authorities to set medically recommended time periods for health services, notify patients who will not be treated within that period for a serious condition, and report related data.

title: Municipal Affairs Statutes Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends property tax regulations to change the rate caps for Class 2 (utility) property in listed municipalities and the regional district tax rate for Class 1 property.

title: Short-Term Rental Accommodations Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Short-Term Rental Accommodations Regulation to change the start date of a prescribed period under the Short-Term Rental Accommodations Act.

title: Short-Term Rental Accommodations Amendment Act (No. 2), 2025
summary: Amends the Short-Term Rental Accommodations Act to let local governments issue temporary permits for short-term rentals in certain circumstances.

title: Interpretation Amendment Act (No. 2), 2025
summary: Repeals section 8.1 of the Interpretation Act, which requires provincial laws to be interpreted as upholding Aboriginal and treaty rights and as consistent with the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.

title: Insurance (Vehicle) Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Insurance (Vehicle) Act to extend the time to claim benefits for catastrophic injuries and reduces the number of amputations required to qualify as a catastrophic injury.

title: Secure Procurement in Respect of China Act
summary: Prohibits public bodies from contracting with suppliers meeting certain criteria related to the People's Republic of China when comparable goods or services are available from Canada or a country with a Canadian trade or economic cooperation agreement.

title: Motor Vehicle Amendment Act (No. 2), 2025
summary: Amends the Motor Vehicle Act to add a driving prohibition for reckless driving, provide for police reporting to the superintendent, and create an offence for driving while prohibited for reckless driving. Reinstated in the 2nd session (2026) at the stage it had reached.

title: Business Practices and Consumer Protection (Greenwashing Prevention) Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Business Practices and Consumer Protection Act to treat certain misleading greenhouse gas or environmental representations as deceptive practices, require disclosure for climate-related claims, and set administrative penalties.

title: Freedom Convoy Recognition Day Act
summary: Designates March 11 as Freedom Convoy Recognition Day and a statutory holiday.

title: Low Carbon Fuels Amendment Act (No. 2), 2025
summary: Amends the Low Carbon Fuels Act to change the carbon intensity reduction used to set targets for jet fuel.

title: Recall and Initiative Amendment Act, 2025
summary: Amends the Recall and Initiative Act to shorten the period after an election during which a recall petition cannot be applied for, and changes recall petition signature requirements.

title: An Act to Ensure the Supremacy of Parliament
summary: A traditional pro forma bill introduced at the opening of each session, before debate on the Speech from the Throne, to assert the Legislative Assembly's right to consider matters other than those raised by the Crown. It is not intended to proceed beyond first reading.

title: Budget Measures Implementation Act, 2026
summary: Implements measures from Budget 2026, including extending the period in which deficits may be forecast to 2028–2029, applying provincial sales tax to accounting, architectural, engineering, non-residential real estate and security services, creating a manufacturing and processing investment tax credit, earlier public accounts deadlines, and making the head of the BC Public Service Agency the merit commissioner.

title: Budget Measures Implementation Act (No. 2), 2026
summary: Establishes the British Columbia Strategic Investments special account and adds related retroactive regulation-making authority.

title: Supply Act (No. 1), 2026
summary: Interim supply bill authorizing government spending for part of the 2026–2027 fiscal year until the main budget estimates are approved.

title: Trade Recognition Act
summary: Replaces Part 1 of the Economic Stabilization (Tariff Response) Act and reduces interprovincial trade barriers by recognizing other provinces' and territories' regulatory measures for the sale and use of goods and the supply of services, subject to exclusions.

title: Motor Vehicle Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Amends the Motor Vehicle Act to allow driver's licence applications in person, online or by other prescribed means, and updates rules on interim licences, duplicate licences, address and email changes, signatures and photos.

title: Post-Secondary International Education (Designated Institutions) Act
summary: Creates a framework for designating and regulating post-secondary institutions that provide programs to international students, including requirements, inspections, enforcement and appeals.

title: Civil Forfeiture Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Amends the Civil Forfeiture Act, including providing for default forfeiture orders where parties fail to respond, changing time periods for the director's actions, and providing for examination for discovery of the director.

title: Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Amends the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, including changes to access request requirements and response timelines, a new exception for communications of judicial officers, expanded grounds to disregard requests, and new information-sharing authority for the commissioner.

title: Labour Statutes Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Amends the Employment Standards Act and Temporary Foreign Worker Protection Act to create a complaint resolution process, allow the director discretion over investigation reports, and require deposits to appeal certain determinations.

title: Residential Tenancy Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Amends the Residential Tenancy Act to add provisions specific to supportive and transitional housing, remove an exemption for certain housing-based health facilities, and add circumstances in which tenancies may be ended.

title: Safe Access to Schools Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Amends the Safe Access to Schools Act to change the date on which the Act is repealed.

title: Safe Access to Places of Public Worship Act
summary: Provides for access zones around places of public worship and prohibits conduct in those zones that impedes access, disrupts activities or causes concern for a person's physical or mental safety.

title: Forests Statutes Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Amends the Forest Act and related statutes, including allowing more stringent terms and conditions in timber sale licences and other authorizations, and creating contract logging authorizations issued by timber sales managers.

title: Environmental Assessment Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Amends the Environmental Assessment Act to add issue resolution protocols and a dispute resolution process, and specifies that a United States tribe may not give notice to participate in the assessment of a project.

title: Miscellaneous Statutes Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Omnibus bill amending multiple statutes, including the Judicial Review Procedure Act (limitation period and Cabinet confidences), the Fuel Price Transparency Act, zero-emission vehicle sales targets, development cost charge waivers, tenancy laws and the Correction Act.

title: Housing and Municipal Affairs Statutes (Codes of Conduct) Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Amends the Community Charter and related statutes to enable a code of conduct for council members with a complaint, investigation and sanction process, and to change certain powers of mayors.

title: Housing and Municipal Affairs Statutes (Parental Leave) Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Amends the Community Charter, Islands Trust Act and Local Government Act to entitle local elected officials to 26 weeks of parental leave without being disqualified from office.

title: K'ómoks Treaty Act
summary: Enacts the K'ómoks Treaty Act and consequential amendments to give effect to and ratify the K'ómoks Treaty, as required under the treaty.

title: Kitselas Treaty Act
summary: Enacts the Kitselas Treaty Act and related amendments to give effect to and ratify the Kitselas Treaty, as required under the treaty.

title: Supply Act, 2026-2027
summary: Main supply bill authorizing government spending from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the 2026–2027 fiscal year, as approved through the budget estimates.

title: Firefighters' Health Act
summary: Requires development of a plan for comprehensive health screening of firefighters, to be tabled in the Legislative Assembly and reviewed every five years, and provides for a review of workers' compensation presumptions for firefighters' occupational diseases such as lung cancer. Reinstated from the 1st session (2025).

title: Professional Reliance Act
summary: Provides for streamlining local government approvals of development projects and reducing their administrative costs, including greater reliance on qualified professionals. Reinstated from the 1st session (2025).

title: Dashboard Cameras in Commercial Vehicles Act
summary: Provides for the mandatory installation and operation of dashboard cameras in commercial vehicles. Reinstated from the 1st session (2025).

title: Motor Vehicle Amendment Act (No. 2), 2025
summary: Amends the Motor Vehicle Act to add a driving prohibition for reckless driving, provide for police reporting to the superintendent, and create an offence for driving while prohibited for reckless driving. Reinstated from the 1st session (2025).

title: Veterans and First Responders Month Act
summary: Establishes November as Veterans and First Responders Month in British Columbia.

title: Long Term Care Access and Transparency Act
summary: Requires health authorities and the minister to report on long-term care waitlists and requires the minister to develop a plan to improve timely access to long-term care.

title: Public Sector Construction Projects Procurement Act
summary: Prohibits solicitations for public sector construction projects that require, or have the effect of requiring, successful vendors to employ unionized or non-unionized workers.

title: School Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Amends the School Act to require boards of education to establish policies on controlled access to school buildings during instructional hours.

title: Drug Recovery and Community Safety Act
summary: Would require cancellation of authorizations and provincial funding for supervised consumption and overdose prevention sites, redirect that funding to recovery and community safety programs, add abstinence conditions to provincial funding agreements, and suspend certain provincial benefits after a drug possession conviction. The bill was ruled out of order.

title: Health Professions and Occupations Repeal Act
summary: Repeals the Health Professions and Occupations Act.

title: Insurance (Vehicle) Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Amends the Insurance (Vehicle) Act to extend the time to claim benefits for catastrophic injuries and reduces the number of amputations required to qualify as a catastrophic injury.

title: Health Professions and Occupations Repeal Act (No. 2)
summary: Repeals the Health Professions and Occupations Act.

title: Aboriginal Title Transparency Act
summary: Requires notice to affected landowners of Aboriginal title claims and negotiations that may affect fee simple land, with notices filed in the land title office, and requires reporting on such claims and negotiations.

title: Transparency of Advocacy Organizations Act
summary: Requires advocacy organizations receiving $10,000 or more a year in provincial, federal or foreign funding to publicly report the amounts and sources, disclose that funding on their websites and social media, and allows residents to apply to court for penalties for contraventions.

title: Interpretation Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Repeals section 8.1 of the Interpretation Act, which requires provincial laws to be interpreted as upholding Aboriginal and treaty rights and as consistent with the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.

title: Mental Health (Brain Injury) Amendment Act, 2026
summary: Amends the Mental Health Act to add a definition of brain injury and include brain injury in the definition of a person with a mental disorder.

title: Speculation and Vacancy Tax Repeal Act
summary: Repeals the Speculation and Vacancy Tax Act while preserving the province's ability to assess and collect tax owed for periods before the repeal.

title: Home Rental Fairness Act
summary: Repeals the Residential Tenancy Act, the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act and the Short-Term Rental Accommodations Act, winds up the Residential Tenancy Branch, and provides a new dispute resolution framework and transitional rules.

title: Young Workers Income Tax Relief Act
summary: Amends the Income Tax Act to reduce provincial income tax payable by individuals under 40 by 50%, and requires the government to reduce total public expenditure by 50% within five years.

title: Small Farms Act
summary: Makes provisions for small farms and small farming cooperatives, including on-site sales and agri-tourism, and requires the minister to publish an annual report.

title: Crown Land and Financial Transparency Act
summary: Requires notice and an opportunity for representations by affected persons before Crown land is disposed of, requires reporting on Crown land dispositions, and establishes a special legislative committee to examine them.

title: Chinese Heritage Month Act
summary: Proclaims February each year as Chinese Heritage Month in British Columbia.

title: Pharmaceutical Risk Management and Accountability Act
summary: Provides for designating classes of experimental drugs and bars practitioners from prescribing or dispensing them unless the wholesaler has a risk management agreement that includes a patient compensation fund and indemnifies the government for certain health costs.
